correctness.rationale: For all fields, homomorphism identities follow from symplectic generator relations. In characteristic two the target Lie bracket has scalar image; wedge rank forces the central image to vanish for n>=2, and the surviving 2-minors yield the rank-one determinantal reduced variety. The rank stratification and singular geometry follow directly. The exhaustive q=2,3,4 checker confirms all four finite cases against direct Lie relations and independent image rank elimination; proof, not enumeration, covers all n and fields.

originality.rationale: The claimed original scope is the characteristic-two higher-rank reduced Hom variety, its singular locus, and exact finite-field image-rank spectra. Ngo 2012 already proves the odd-characteristic commuting determinant locus and Berkeley 2010 documents the small characteristic-two faithful example; both are explicitly antecedents, not novelty claims. Rojas 2012 addresses minimal faithful dimensions in characteristic zero. Direct full-text comparison and relevant record searches identified no stronger result covering the new combined char-2 conclusions. Historical completeness remains a risk.
residual_risks: Unsearched historical modular Lie-representation classifications may present a stronger equivalent result under representation-scheme, commuting-scheme or determinantal language.
A general identity for maps between two-step nilpotent Lie algebras might recover the classification as a special case; no such source was identified in the inspected primary literature.
The scheme-theoretic nilpotent structure when n>=2 is not analyzed; the geometric classification is expressly reduced.

value.rationale: This computes an exact natural representation-space invariant for all higher Heisenberg ranks in characteristic two, including complete rank-resolved finite-field counts and singular-locus dimensions. The dimension jump at characteristic two and the sharp n=1 faithful boundary are structurally motivated. The result is not a random small sample, changed notation, or a mere repetition of known odd-characteristic commuting-variety results.
